title: weakness-registry-v2 lane threat list
description: One file per language lane: code/specs/data/weakness-registry-v2/lanes/<lang>.json. See VER15a section 6. The schema checks shape only; the cross-checks (every registry v2 CWE has a threat, evidence ids resolve, file:line refs exist) are the validator's job, listed in VER15a section 9.

lane.description: Must equal the file name without .json.

family.description: Language family, which decides which evidence kinds may close which classes (VER15a section 5).

sources.description: Where the lane-specific classes came from (a MITRE view, the language specification, a prior CVE study).

toolchain.description: The compilers or interpreters the evidence is produced with, so a claim names what it ran under.

considered_not_included.description: Weakness classes from the named sources that were considered and left out, each with the reason. An empty list is allowed only if every source class is in threats.

packages.description: Per-package status of every threat. Keys are package names within the lane (for example logic-gates).

label.description: Proof labels, weakest to strongest (VER31 section 4). none means no evidence of that row exists yet.

id.description: Stable id the validator resolves, such as analyzer-rule:c.no-pointer-types or sanitizer-run:asan+ubsan.

state.description: live: a repository tool checks it on every build or report. planned: named work item, not yet live. unverified: an attestation no tool checks (rendered with the words 'not machine-checked').

planned_item.description: Backlog id; required when state is planned.

origin.description: registry-v2: one of the 29 registry classes (cwe required). lane: a class the language adds.

cwe.description: Required (an integer) for origin registry-v2; may be null for a lane threat with no CWE.

rationale.description: Why this class is a plausible weakness in THIS language for a gate-like package, in plain prose.

applicability.description: applicable: the language has no structural barrier. applicable-in-principle: the language permits it but a package-level restriction can close it. not-applicable: the language cannot express it (then closed_by names the language guarantee).

closed_by.description: The checks that close the class, in the order a reader should trust them. A class with an empty list is invalid.

exclude_requires.description: Ids from closed_by that must ALL be live for status excluded.

discharge_requires.description: Ids from closed_by that must ALL be live, with the evidence reaching floor_label, for status discharged.

floor_label.description: The label a discharge must reach. Registry classes default to the registry's minimum_proof_label.

threat.description: A threat id of this file.

reached.description: The strongest label the lane's own evidence for this row reaches today.

reason.description: Why the row has this status. For open rows it is rendered after the word 'open:' in a release.

ref.description: file:line, a BUILD line, a PR number or a spec section: something a reader can open.

becomes_when.description: For an open row: the planned closure ids (and backlog items) that, once live, turn it into excluded or discharged. Required when status is open and any planned closure item exists.

becomes_status.description: Status the row will have when becomes_when has landed.

reviewed_at_commit.description: A commit hash, or pr-<n> while the package is not yet on main.

scope.description: Which files the rows speak about (library sources, not the tests).
